questions.q: Walk me through your career and why you're looking at this role now.
questions.hint: Two minutes, in order: Infosys (SoW, billing and timesheets for 200 resources), then PMO at Accenture and KPIT, then Scrum Master at JPMorgan (5 teams), Maersk GSC (BI Finance), B/S/H (supported the RTE across 5 teams), and now CBA (5 CDAO workstreams). End on the move you want next, toward the scope this role offers.

questions.q: Why a GCC, and why this company in particular?
questions.hint: You've spent most of your career inside GCCs (JPMorgan, Maersk GSC, CBA), so you know how onshore–offshore ownership works. Name one thing from the JD or the company's India expansion news and link it to what you've delivered.

questions.q: What's your biggest achievement as a Scrum Master or delivery lead?
questions.hint: Pick a STAR story with a number, for example cutting sprint spillover at CBA through Scrum of Scrums and pre-BRP dependency mapping. Situation → what you changed → the measurable result (add your figure).

questions.q: Tell me about a time a delivery went wrong. What did you learn?
questions.hint: Choose a real miss: a release slip, a late dependency or an unclear story. Own your part, explain the fix (e.g. the DoR/DoD you introduced at B/S/H), and show the practice you've kept since.

questions.q: Where do you see yourself in three years?
questions.hint: Your resume already signals the direction: from Scrum Master to Technical Program Manager or RTE for data and AI programs. Mention the Agentic AI (IIT Madras) and SAFe learning as proof you're investing in it.

questions.q: How do you prepare for and run PI Planning (or a quarterly Big Room Planning)?
questions.hint: Use CBA's quarterly BRP: before the event you mapped task sequences, owners and cross-team dependencies through Scrum of Scrums, so the room focused on decisions. Cover readiness (features refined, capacity known), the dependency board, the risk ROAM, and confidence voting.

questions.q: What does a Release Train Engineer do that a Scrum Master doesn't?
questions.hint: Train-level flow versus team-level flow: the ART sync, PI objectives, the program board, inspect & adapt, and coaching Scrum Masters. Mention supporting the RTE at B/S/H across five product teams and running Scrum of Scrums at CBA, so you've done much of it already.

questions.q: How do you handle a team that keeps missing its PI objectives?
questions.hint: Separate the cause: over-commitment, unplanned work, dependencies or unclear features. Show the data you'd look at (planned vs actual business value, spillover), then the change: capacity buffers, earlier dependency calls, better feature readiness.

questions.q: Which SAFe events have you facilitated, and how did you adapt them to your organisation?
questions.hint: Be specific: Scrum of Scrums, BRP/PI planning, system demos, retrospectives. Leading SAFe 6.0 (2024) shows you know the framework; your adaptations show judgement, e.g. a lighter SoS cadence for data-platform workstreams.

questions.q: How do you make backlog refinement effective when stories keep arriving incomplete?
questions.hint: B/S/H story: you brought in Definition of Ready across five Scrum teams and ran JAD sessions with POs and business teams, which cut repeated discussions. Describe the DoR checklist and how you got POs to adopt it.

questions.q: A team treats stand-ups as status meetings for the manager. What do you do?
questions.hint: Coach the purpose (plan the next 24 hours, raise blockers), change the format (walk the board right to left), and agree with the manager to step back. Mention working agreements you reinforced at Maersk and JPMorgan.

questions.q: How do you run a retrospective that leads to real change?
questions.hint: Vary the formats, focus on one or two actions with owners, and review them at the next retro. You shared retro findings with other Scrum Masters at JPMorgan to spread improvements, so use that as your example.

questions.q: How do you coach a new Product Owner?
questions.hint: Prioritisation (value vs effort, WSJF), writing acceptance criteria, saying no, and joining refinement. Tie it to your PO pairing at B/S/H and CBA.

questions.q: How do you manage dependencies across several teams or workstreams?
questions.hint: Your strongest topic. At CBA you coordinate five CDAO workstreams (Tableau, AWB MEP, Alteryx, Vulnerability Management, Alation): a dependency map before BRP, owners and dates in Scrum of Scrums, escalation when a date is at risk. Give one example of a dependency you unblocked.

questions.q: Show me how you keep a RAID log useful rather than a document nobody reads.
questions.hint: Owners, due dates, a weekly review in governance forums, and only the top risks surfaced to leadership. Mention the KPI and RAID monitoring you do at CBA and your PMO experience with HP PPM at KPIT.

questions.q: When do you escalate, and how?
questions.hint: Escalate when a team can't resolve something within its own authority before it hits a milestone. Bring options, not just the problem. Give a CBA example of escalating an unresolved dependency or resourcing risk and the outcome.

questions.q: How do you report program status to senior leadership?
questions.hint: One page: an honest RAG status, milestones, the top three risks with asks, and decisions needed. You've done monthly status and KPI trend reports since Accenture, and governance reviews at CBA.

questions.q: Tell me about a disagreement with a senior stakeholder over scope or timelines.
questions.hint: STAR: show the data you used (capacity, dependencies), the trade-off you offered (scope vs date), and how the relationship stayed intact. Pick a release-readiness or BRP-priority example.

questions.q: How do you work with onshore teams in another time zone (e.g. Australia, US, UK)?
questions.hint: CBA (Australia), JPMorgan and Maersk all involved distributed teams. Cover overlap hours, written updates, clear decision owners, and building trust with the onshore product leads.

questions.q: Which delivery metrics do you track, and how do you avoid them being gamed?
questions.hint: Say/do ratio or predictability, spillover, cycle time, throughput and escaped defects, used for team improvement, never to compare teams. Mention the delivery KPIs you monitor at CBA and the dashboards you built with pivot tables and IPM+.

questions.q: How have you improved a team's predictability?
questions.hint: Use numbers: spillover before and after, unplanned work reduced by mapping dependencies before BRP. If you don't have exact figures, give honest approximations and say how you measured them.

questions.q: What would your first 90-day dashboard for this program show?
questions.hint: Milestone burn-up, dependency status, risk heatmap, team predictability, release readiness. Mention automating the reporting, as your CBA process-automation work did.

questions.q: How do you build a program plan when requirements are still unclear?
questions.hint: Plan in layers: fixed milestones and dates, rolling-wave detail, assumptions logged as risks, and re-planning at each increment. Mention integrated planning and milestone tracking from your PMO years.

questions.q: How do you balance BAU work against roadmap delivery for the same team?
questions.hint: Make the BAU load visible, reserve capacity for it, use a separate Kanban lane, and review it quarterly. Your CBA platform teams juggle vulnerability fixes and support alongside roadmap work, so use them as the example.

questions.q: Tell me about a program you took from start to finish.
questions.hint: Choose your strongest: a CBA workstream like the Alation data-catalogue rollout. Cover scope, the teams involved, key milestones, risks you managed and the outcome.

questions.q: Walk me through how you get a release production-ready.
questions.hint: At CBA you oversee release coordination, change approvals, production readiness and support handovers across platform teams. Describe your checklist: testing sign-off, CAB/change approval, rollback plan, support handover, comms.

questions.q: A critical release is at risk two days before go-live. What do you do?
questions.hint: Triage the issue, assess impact, give the decision-makers options (go with mitigation, go with reduced scope, slip), and communicate early. Show your ServiceNow/ITIL change and incident knowledge.

questions.q: How is delivering an AI/ML or GenAI program different from a normal software program?
questions.hint: Experimentation and uncertainty (model performance isn't guaranteed), data readiness as a dependency, evaluation criteria, MLOps (serving, monitoring, drift), and responsible-AI review. Draw on your IIT Madras Agentic AI programme and IBM RAG/LangChain certificates.

questions.q: Have you used AI to improve delivery or your own work?
questions.hint: Yes: describe a concrete use, like the process automation at CBA, or AI agents you've built in your coursework (LangChain, LangGraph, n8n) for status summaries or RAID updates. Interviewers at Walmart and Target explicitly look for this.

questions.q: Explain RAG or an AI agent to a business stakeholder in one minute.
questions.hint: RAG: the model looks up your company's documents before it answers, so its replies are grounded and current. Agent: a model that can plan steps and use tools to finish a task. Keep it plain, then give a use case from banking or retail.

questions.q: How do you define 'done' and success criteria for an AI feature?
questions.hint: Agree evaluation metrics before the build (accuracy, latency, cost, a human-rated quality sample), add guardrail and safety checks, run a pilot with real users, and monitor after release.

questions.q: Tell me about your data-governance or data-platform experience.
questions.hint: CBA CDAO: aligned teams on Alation data-catalogue initiatives (metadata management, data ownership, governance requirements), plus Tableau and Alteryx platform workstreams. Explain why governance needs owners and adoption, not just a tool.

questions.q: How do you manage dependencies on upstream data that your team doesn't own?
questions.hint: Data contracts or agreed SLAs, an early readiness check, an escalation path, and tracking it as a named dependency in the RAID log. Give a CDAO example.

questions.q: How would you run a legacy-to-cloud migration program?
questions.hint: Inventory and wave planning, landing-zone readiness, dual running and cut-over, rollback, and decommissioning. You hold AWS Cloud Practitioner and know CI/CD, Docker and observability concepts (CloudWatch, Prometheus, Grafana), so use them to show you can ask the right technical questions.

questions.q: How technical are you? How do you earn engineers' trust as a non-coding lead?
questions.hint: Be honest: not hands-on, but technically fluent (Python basics, Git, AWS, CI/CD, MLOps concepts). You earn trust by protecting focus time, clearing blockers fast and asking good questions in design reviews.

questions.q: Tell me about your vulnerability-management or security-program work.
questions.hint: CBA: you review vulnerability reports, assess issues by criticality and route priority items to SMEs for remediation and follow-up. Describe how you tracked remediation SLAs and reported status.

questions.q: How do you deliver in a regulated environment without slowing teams down?
questions.hint: Build controls into the Definition of Done, have evidence ready for audits, involve risk partners early, and automate compliance checks. Banking GCCs (CBA, JPMorgan) give you direct examples.

questions.q: Have you managed people? How would you lead a team of Scrum Masters or TPMs?
questions.hint: Be honest about formal line management versus leading through influence. Give examples of mentoring, coaching new Scrum Masters, and hiring or onboarding. Then describe how you'd set goals, run 1:1s and grow people.

questions.q: How do you handle an under-performing team member?
questions.hint: Clarify expectations, understand the cause, agree a plan with checkpoints, give support, and document it. Keep it fair and private.

questions.q: How would you raise agile maturity across teams that are at different levels?
questions.hint: Assess each team, agree a small set of shared standards (DoR/DoD, working agreements), coach team by team, and keep a Scrum Master community of practice. Your DoR/DoD rollout across five teams at B/S/H is the proof.

questions.q: A senior leader says 'agile isn't working here'. How do you respond?
questions.hint: Ask what outcome they're missing, show data, suggest one targeted fix and a time-boxed trial. Avoid defending the framework for its own sake.

questions.q: How do you do capacity planning and resource forecasting?
questions.hint: Your PMO roots: you forecast resource demand with the APMO team at KPIT, managed capacity at CBA, and handled billing and utilisation for 200 resources at Infosys. Explain how you match demand to capacity and flag gaps early.

questions.q: How do you manage a program budget or vendor?
questions.hint: Track budget against actuals and forecast monthly, use SoW-based vendor governance with clear deliverables and acceptance, and raise variance early. Your SoW and billing work at Infosys (Apple account) is relevant.

questions.q: What's different about delivery in a bank compared with other industries?
questions.hint: Regulation, change control, risk and audit, legacy systems and high-availability needs. Use CBA and JPMorgan examples, and show you can move fast inside the controls.

questions.q: Which banking or financial-services business areas have you supported?
questions.hint: Name them accurately: CBA's CDAO data and analytics platforms; JPMorgan's teams (name the line of business you supported); Maersk BI Finance. Link each to the domain in this JD.

questions.q: How do you set up Jira or Azure DevOps so it actually helps the program?
questions.hint: A consistent issue hierarchy (epic → feature → story), clear workflows, dependency links, dashboards for leadership, and automation rules for hygiene. You've used Jira, Confluence, ADO and Rally, plus PPM tools like HP PPM and Clarity.
